# Lab 6.1: Time-Unit Column Partitioning

## What We Are Going to Do
Build a non-partitioned table and a daily-partitioned copy of taxi data, then measure how much less data a date filter reads.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Create the dataset.**

<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq --location=US mk --dataset $PROJECT_ID:lab06</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Create the two tables.** This reads a few GB once from the public table.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE TABLE lab06.trips_flat AS
SELECT unique_key, taxi_id, trip_start_timestamp, trip_seconds, trip_miles, fare, tips, payment_type, company
FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`
WHERE trip_start_timestamp &gt;= '2023-01-01' AND trip_start_timestamp &lt; '2024-01-01';

CREATE TABLE lab06.trips_daily
PARTITION BY DATE(trip_start_timestamp)
AS SELECT * FROM lab06.trips_flat;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Compare a one-day query.** Run each and read **Bytes processed**.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(fare) FROM lab06.trips_flat
WHERE DATE(trip_start_timestamp) = '2023-07-04';

SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(fare) FROM lab06.trips_daily
WHERE DATE(trip_start_timestamp) = '2023-07-04';</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The partitioned table reads about 1/365 of the data.

4. **[Console] Create a monthly-partitioned table in the UI.** On `lab06` click **Create table**:
   - **Source**: Empty table, **Table**: `trips_monthly`
   - Add the same schema, or use **Edit as text** and paste a few columns
   - **Partitioning**: Partition by field `trip_start_timestamp`, **By month**

5. **[CLI] Create an hourly-partitioned table with bq.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --destination_table=lab06.trips_hourly \
  --time_partitioning_field=trip_start_timestamp --time_partitioning_type=HOUR \
  'SELECT * FROM lab06.trips_flat WHERE trip_start_timestamp &lt; "2023-02-01"'
bq show --format=prettyjson lab06.trips_hourly | grep -A3 timePartitioning</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


6. **[SQL] A filter that breaks pruning.** Partition pruning needs a filter on the partition column itself:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT COUNT(*) FROM lab06.trips_daily
WHERE EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM trip_start_timestamp) = 1;   -- scans every partition</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Daily partitions | 365 partitions for 2023 |
| One-day query | ~1/365 of the bytes of the flat table |
| Granularity | Hour, day, month or year |
| Pruning | Only with a direct filter on the partition column |
